transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Um, thank you for taking the time to see me. I really appreciate it. I hope I'm explaining this right... I guess I'm here because things have been a little, well, stressful at my job. I'm a transportation inspector. I actually just got this county safety award recently, which I was really proud of, you know? I always try to do things exactly by the book and be a good employee. 

But ever since that award... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being difficult, I really don't, but certain people at work have been sort of twisting my inspection reports. They keep asking these really pointed budget questions, almost like they're trying to make me look crooked. 

I did talk to my supervisor, and he says it's just a normal review. And I want to believe him, I try so hard to be a team player, but... I can just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. I know that might sound heavy, and I hope it's okay that I'm bringing this up to you. I just want to figure out how to handle it so I can keep doing good work. Does that make sense? Is that something you can help me with?

You mentioned your supervisor told you it's a normal review. When he said that, did that help reassure you, or do you still feel quite certain that there's a coordinated effort against you despite what he said?

Well, I really wanted it to reassure me. I mean, I respect my supervisor a lot, and I don't want to be the guy who questions management, you know? I want to be easy to work with. So when he said it was just a normal review, I tried—I really tried—to just accept it and go back to my desk and do my job. 

But... I don't know, I hope this doesn't make me sound paranoid or anything, but I just can't shake it. It's the way they're doing it. The pointed questions about the budget, the way my reports are being twisted... it just doesn't feel like a standard review. I really don't want to cause trouble, but I feel pretty certain that there's this coordinated effort to discredit me, especially after I won that award. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds bad, like I'm not trusting my boss. Do you think it's wrong of me to feel that way? I just want to protect my reputation so I can keep being a good employee.

If I told you that multiple trusted colleagues, not just your supervisor, had reviewed the situation and all agreed there was no coordinated effort against you, do you think you could accept that, or would you still believe the effort was real?

Oh, wow. Um... I would really, really want to accept that. I mean, if my colleagues said that, I'd want to just nod and say, 'Okay, my mistake,' because I hate being difficult. I really do. I always want to be a team player. 

But... and I hope it's okay to be completely honest with you here... I don't think I could just accept it. Because I'm the one seeing it happen firsthand, you know? I'm the one watching them twist my inspection reports and dealing with those really pointed budget questions. It's like... ever since I got that county safety award, they're just trying to make me look crooked. 

So even if my supervisor and a bunch of colleagues told me it was just a normal review, deep down, I can just tell there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. I can feel it. I know that probably isn't the answer you're looking for... does that make me sound stubborn? I really don't mean to be, I just... I know what I'm seeing. Is it okay that I feel that way?

On a scale where 1 means you're completely certain this coordinated effort is real and 0 means you think it's definitely not real, where would you say you fall right now? Is there any part of you that wonders if maybe you could be mistaken about this?

Um... on that scale? I guess... I really wish I could tell you I'm at a zero. I want to be at a zero so badly, because I'd love to just be mistaken about all this. I try to tell myself that I'm just overthinking it, because I want to be an easygoing guy. 

But if I'm being completely honest—and I hope it's okay to just be straight with you—I think I'd have to say I'm at a 1. 

It's just that I see it happening every day. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people at work have been twisting my inspection reports. And they keep asking these really pointed budget questions, almost like they're trying to make me look crooked. Even when my supervisor tells me it's just a normal review, and I try so hard to just smile and accept that, I can still tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably makes me sound really stubborn, and I promise I'm not trying to be a difficult patient or employee. I just can't ignore what they're doing to my work. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions okay.

Before this situation at work started, have you ever had similar feelings in other areas of your life—like in relationships with family or friends, or in other jobs—where you felt like people were coordinating against you or trying to harm your reputation?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um... I've always gotten along really well with pretty much everyone. 

My family and my friends, we're all great. I'm usually the one trying to keep the peace if there's ever a disagreement, you know? I want everyone to be happy. And at my old jobs, before I became an inspector, I always had really good relationships with my coworkers and bosses. I was always the guy happy to pick up an extra shift or help out. I've never, ever felt like anyone was out to get me before this. 

That's why this whole thing right now is just so... so upsetting to me. It's completely new. I'm really not the kind of guy who goes around looking for trouble or thinking people are against me. I just want to do a good job and go home. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, I hope that helps you see I'm normally a really easygoing person. Did I explain that okay?

When you're not at work—like at home in the evenings or on weekends—do you find yourself thinking about this coordinated effort against you, or is it mainly something that's on your mind when you're actually at your job?

Um... I do think about it sometimes when I'm at home, mostly because I just want to do a good job and it bothers me that they're twisting things. But I really try not to let it take over my whole life, you know? 

I mean, I hope it's okay to say this, but I feel like I'm still handling everything pretty well. I still get to work on time every day, I complete all my inspections just like I'm supposed to, and I still keep up with church on Sundays. I make sure I'm taking care of myself, eating right, keeping the house clean... I'm really trying to be responsible about it all. 

The main problems really only come up when people bring up those reports or start questioning my spending at work. That's when I get a little... flustered, I guess. But otherwise, I'm just living my normal life. I hope that shows that I'm trying my best to not let this affect everything else. Does that sound like I'm handling it okay?

When your coworkers ask you those budget questions or make comments about your reports, do you think they're specifically trying to target you because of the award you won, or do you think they might be asking those same questions of other inspectors too—you just happen to notice it more when it's directed at you?

Um... well, I really wish I could say they were just treating everyone the same. I want to believe that, I really do. It would make things so much easier, right? 

But... um, I've watched them with the other inspectors. They don't get asked these same pointed budget questions. And their inspection reports don't get twisted around. It really is just me. 

And it's... it's definitely because of that county safety award. I know it sounds like maybe I'm being a little sensitive, and I'm really trying not to be, I promise. But ever since I got that recognition, it's like a switch flipped. They're trying to make me look crooked, like I don't deserve the award or my job. 

I know my supervisor says it's just a normal review, and I nod and go along with it because I want to be a good employee and not cause a fuss... but deep down, I can just tell there's this coordinated effort to discredit me. It's really hard to ignore when it's directed right at you, you know? 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining too much. I'm just trying to be honest about what I'm seeing. Is it okay that I feel that way?

If you were to imagine the most charitable explanation for what's happening—like maybe the budget questions are routine and your supervisor really was being honest—how much effort would it take you to actually believe that explanation, even temporarily?

Um... wow, that's... that's a really good question. I mean, I try to be a reasonable person, I really do. I want to be easy to work with.

If I try really hard to think about it like that... like maybe the budget questions really are just routine, and maybe my supervisor is telling the truth about it just being a normal review... um... 

I guess I can sort of picture it in my head? Like, I can understand the words. But... oh, I hope this doesn't make me sound stubborn, because I promise I'm not trying to be difficult... but to actually *believe* it? It's just really, really hard. 

Because I look at what's actually happening, you know? Ever since I got that county safety award, the way they twist my inspection reports and ask those pointed questions... it just feels so obvious that they're trying to make me look crooked. Even when my supervisor tells me it's normal, I just... I can just tell there's this coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I want to believe the charitable explanation, I really do. It would be so much nicer if everyone was just doing their jobs. But I just can't shake what I'm seeing with my own eyes. I'm sorry, I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to be completely honest with you.

When your coworkers ask those budget questions or twist your reports, do you think they're deliberately trying to send you a message or signal something to you, or do you think they're just trying to make you look bad in a more straightforward way?

Um... I think... well, I don't think they're trying to send me a secret message or anything like that. I'm not... I know that would sound a bit crazy, and I'm definitely not thinking like that, I promise. 

I think it's just... it's just a very straightforward thing. Ever since I got that county safety award, they're just twisting my inspection reports and asking those pointed budget questions because they want to make me look crooked to the higher-ups. Like I said, even when my supervisor says it's just a normal review, I can just tell there's this coordinated effort to discredit me and make me look bad on paper. 

They just want me to look like I don't know what I'm doing, or like I'm doing something wrong with the money. It's nothing... nothing weird or coded. Just people being unfair. I hope that makes sense? I'm just trying to be really clear that I don't think they're sending me signals or anything, just that they're trying to ruin my reputation. Does that sound like a reasonable way to look at it?

When you think about the budget questions and the way your reports are being handled, do you think it's possible that some of what you're interpreting as a coordinated effort could actually just be normal workplace procedures that you're reading as targeted because you're upset about something, or do you feel completely certain that there is definitely a real coordinated effort happening?

Um... well, I really wish I could say it was just normal procedures. I know that's what my supervisor keeps telling me, and I know that's probably what you'd like to hear, too. I really want to be the kind of employee who just accepts that and doesn't cause any problems.

But... um... I just can't. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds bad. But I'm completely certain. It's just... it's so clear to me. Ever since I won that county safety award, the way they twist my inspection reports and keep asking those same pointed budget questions... it's not just me being upset or reading into things. They really are trying to make me look crooked. 

I know it might sound like I'm just being difficult, and I promise I'm really trying not to be. But I can just tell there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. It's really happening. I hope you're not disappointed in me for saying that... I just have to be honest about what I'm experiencing. Is it okay that I'm so sure about it?

You mentioned that your supervisor and colleagues have all said this is just a normal review. In your heart of hearts, is there even a small part of you that thinks they might actually be right and you could be mistaken about this coordinated effort, or do you feel absolutely certain they're wrong and you're right?

Um... wow, you're really pushing me to think about this from every angle, aren't you? Which is good, I mean, I appreciate that you're so thorough. I really want to give you the right answer here... the one that shows I'm being reasonable.

But... in my heart of hearts? Um... no. I don't think I'm mistaken. I really don't. 

I know they all say it's just a normal review. My supervisor tells me that, and the others act like it's just business as usual. And I know it would be so much easier for everyone, including me, if I just nodded along and said, "Okay, you're right, I'm just being paranoid." I really wish I could just do that and be the easygoing guy I want to be.

But I can't ignore what's happening. The timeline is just too specific, you know? It all started right after that county safety award. And the way they twist the inspection reports, the specific budget questions they ask... it's all designed to make me look crooked. 

I feel absolutely certain that there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. I know they're wrong when they say it's normal, and I know I'm right about what they're doing. 

I'm really sorry if that's not what you were hoping to hear. I know it probably makes me sound really inflexible, and I hate that. I just... I have to trust what I'm seeing, right? I hope you can understand why I'm so sure about this. Am I making sense?

If I were to tell you that I've reviewed your case carefully and I genuinely believe you're misinterpreting normal workplace procedures as a coordinated effort against you, would any part of you consider that I might be right, or would you be completely confident that I'm wrong and you're right?

Um... wow. I... I really respect your opinion, doctor. I know you're the expert here, and you've probably seen so many things like this. I really, really want to be the kind of patient who just listens to their doctor and says, "Yes, you're right, I'll work on that." That's the kind of person I try to be. 

But... if you told me that... I think I would just feel really misunderstood. I'm sorry, I don't mean to be disrespectful at all! I just... I know what I'm living through every day. 

I know it sounds like I'm just being stubborn, but I'm completely confident that I'm right about this. It's just so obvious to me. Before that county safety award, everything was fine. And now, the way they twist my inspection reports... the way they keep asking those pointed budget questions... it's not just normal procedures. They are trying to make me look crooked. Even when my supervisor says it's normal, I can just tell there's this coordinated effort to discredit me. 

I really hate disagreeing with you, I do. It makes me feel like I'm failing as a patient or something. But I have to be honest about what they're doing to me at work. I know I'm right about it. I hope you're not mad at me for saying that... I'm just trying to be truthful with you. Is it okay that we disagree on this?

If it turned out that you were wrong about this coordinated effort—if you somehow discovered concrete proof that it wasn't real—do you think you'd be able to accept that and change your mind, or do you think you'd find a way to explain away that proof?

Um... wow, that's a really tough question. I want to say yes. I really, really want to be the kind of person who can just look at evidence and say, "Oh, okay, I was wrong, my mistake." I know that's the healthy way to be, and I promise I try to be reasonable like that. 

But... um... I just don't know how that could even happen. I'm sorry, I don't want to sound like I'm being difficult or closed-minded. It's just that the proof of what they're doing is already so concrete to me. 

Like, I know you're asking a hypothetical, and I really want to give you a good answer... but I just keep coming back to the facts. Before the county safety award, none of this was happening. And now, the way they twist those inspection reports, and the specific budget questions they ask... it's all so clearly aimed at making me look crooked. Even when my supervisor insists it's just a normal review, I can just tell there's this coordinated effort to discredit me. 

So... if someone showed me "proof" that it wasn't happening... I think I'd have to wonder where that proof came from. Because the people trying to discredit me are pretty thorough. I guess I'd probably think the proof was just part of the effort to cover it all up. 

I'm really sorry, I know that sounds terrible and probably makes me seem really paranoid. I hate that I'm giving you an answer that makes me look bad. I just want to be completely honest with you about how my mind is working with all of this. I hope you're not too frustrated with me for saying that... am I being too stubborn?
